transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Well... I guess what finally scared me enough to make an appointment is what's been happening on my shifts. I work surveillance, you know, watching the floor monitors. I actually have a bachelor's degree, which is kind of funny because sitting in a dark room staring at screens isn't exactly what I thought I'd be doing at 44. My mother always said I should have gone into teaching, but kids just exhaust me, and the casino pays decently enough. 

Anyway, during the really quiet stretches in the surveillance room... I've started hearing these voices coming through the monitor speakers. They keep saying things to me, like, "You missed it, Ruth," or... or "People are going to get hurt because of you." And I'm always so careful with my job. I even brought in my own lumbar support pillow last week because those company chairs just destroy your lower back if you sit for ten hours straight, you know? 

But the voices... every single channel on my console is completely muted. I double-check the dials every time. And when the other officers walk in for their rounds, they don't hear anything at all. No one else hears it but me.
Have you noticed any other unusual sights, sounds, or sensations that others around you don’t seem to notice, outside of what you’ve described hearing on the monitors?

No, I don't think so. It's really just the monitors in the surveillance room. I haven't seen anything that isn't there, or felt anything strange. Just those voices when I'm sitting at the console. 

It's a really isolating room, you know? They keep it absolutely freezing in there, too, because of all the equipment. I have to wear this thick wool cardigan that my sister knit for me for Christmas a few years ago. She's really gotten into knitting ever since her youngest went off to college. She made me a scarf, too, but it's this awful mustard yellow color that completely washes out my complexion. I mean, I appreciate the thought, she spent a lot of time on it, but I just can't wear it out of the house. I just leave it shoved in my locker at the casino. The employee lockers are so tiny, though, you can barely fit a winter coat in them, let alone a giant chunky scarf and my lunch bag. I usually bring a turkey sandwich, but deli meat has gotten so expensive lately... 

I'm sorry, what were you asking me? Oh, right, the unusual things. No, nothing else like that. Just the voices from the speakers at work.
Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs that others might not share or find hard to believe, such as feeling like you're being watched, followed, or targeted in some way?

Watched? No... no, I don't think so. Honestly, I'm the one doing the watching, right? That's the irony of it. I'm the one staring at the cameras all day. You really see everything from up there. People think they're being so sneaky when they try to swipe a chip or whatever, but the cameras catch it all. 

The resolution on those new overhead cameras they put in is incredible. They installed them last spring, right around the time the casino replaced all the carpeting on the main floor. They chose this hideous geometric pattern—red and gold and black. I read somewhere once that casinos pick ugly carpets on purpose so people keep their eyes up and looking at the slot machines. It makes sense, I guess, but it gives me a terrible headache if I stare at it too long on the monitors. I actually get headaches pretty easily if the lighting is bad, which is why I always keep a bottle of ibuprofen in my purse. I buy the big generic bottles from Costco because the name brand is just a rip-off, you know? It's the exact same active ingredient. My mother refuses to believe that, she'll only buy Advil. She's so stubborn about the weirdest things. 

But anyway... no, I don't feel like anyone is targeting me or following me or anything like that. Just going to work and going home.
Have there been times when you believed something strongly that others didn’t seem to agree with or thought was strange, even though you felt certain it was true?

Well... I don't know if other people think it's strange, but I just know it's true. I keep replaying every single missed camera angle in my head, or any time I've had a delayed call down to the floor. It's just absolute proof to me that I am completely careless and... and dangerous, really. Part of me strongly believes that I deserve to be punished if anything goes wrong on my watch. 

Speaking of watches, I actually had to stop wearing mine because the clasp kept catching on the sleeve of that wool cardigan I told you about. It's a real shame because it was a beautiful Seiko watch. My dad gave it to me when I got my degree. He was so proud. He bought it at this little jeweler downtown that isn't even there anymore. The whole block got bought out and turned into a strip mall with a boutique coffee shop. Not a Starbucks, one of those trendy places that charges seven dollars for an oat milk latte. I really don't understand how people afford to buy coffee out every single day in this economy. I just make mine at home with a standard drip machine. I buy the big tub of Folgers from the grocery store. It gets the job done, you know? Though my coffee maker is starting to make this awful sputtering noise in the mornings, so I might need to descale it with some white vinegar. You have to run the water through like three times afterward, though, or your coffee tastes like salad dressing... 

I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought again. But yes, I just... I know I'm careless. I just feel like I'm a danger to everyone there and I deserve whatever punishment is coming to me.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports auditory hallucinations limited to a specific context (surveillance monitors) and without external corroboration. There is no evidence of delusions, disorganized thinking, or other primary psychotic symptoms outside of the context of the hallucinations. The patient also shows insight into other aspects of her life and does not demonstrate broad impairment in reality testing, which makes F20.9 (Schizophrenia, unspecified) and F25.9 (Schizoaffective disorder, unspecified) less likely. The clinical picture is more consistent with F23.9 (Acute and transient psychotic disorder), likely a brief psychotic reaction confined to a specific environmental context.
